ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a vertex-edge schematic diagram of a regular icosahedron, with vertex A at the very top, vertex Z at the very bottom, and Z directly opposite A. Between A and Z, it can be seen that there are two rings, upper and lower, each with 5 vertices; the solid and dashed edges indicate traversable edges. In the figure, A is adjacent to the 5 vertices in the upper ring, Z is adjacent to the 5 vertices in the lower ring, and these intermediate vertices also have connections within the same layer or adjacent layers. Reasoning: Layer by graph distance to Z: Z is layer 0; the 5 vertices adjacent to Z are layer 1; the next upper ring of 5 vertices is layer 2; A is layer 3. Let E0=0, E1 be the expected remaining number of steps from any vertex in layer 1 to reach Z, and E2 be the expected remaining number of steps from any vertex in layer 2 to reach Z. In each step Annie can only choose an edge that does not move farther from Z, and chooses uniformly at random among all valid edges. Starting from a layer 1 vertex, there are 3 valid edges: 1 to Z and 2 to the same layer. Therefore E1 = 1 + (2/3)E1, solving gives E1 = 3. Starting from a layer 2 vertex, there are 4 valid edges: 2 to layer 1 and 2 to layer 2. Therefore E2 = 1 + (1/2)E1 + (1/2)E2. Substituting E1=3 gives E2 = 1 + 3/2 + E2/2, so E2=5. Starting from A, all valid first steps go to layer 2, therefore EA = 1 + E2 = 6.

Starting from a layer 1 vertex, there are 3 valid edges: 1 to Z and 2 to the same layer. Therefore E1 = 1 + (2/3)E1, solving gives E1 = 3.

Starting from a layer 2 vertex, there are 4 valid edges: 2 to layer 1 and 2 to layer 2. Therefore E2 = 1 + (1/2)E1 + (1/2)E2. Substituting E1=3 gives E2 = 1 + 3/2 + E2/2, so E2=5.

Starting from A, all valid first steps go to layer 2, therefore EA = 1 + E2 = 6.
